elements.element: Audit frequency is limited to no more than once in any 12-month period.
elements.evidence: The clause states that an audit “shall take place no more than once in any twelve (12) month period.”

elements.element: Customer receives at least 30 days' prior written notice.
elements.evidence: The clause requires “not less than thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Licensee.”

elements.element: The audit occurs during business hours.
elements.evidence: The clause requires the audit to occur “during normal business hours.”

elements.element: The audit is conducted by an independent auditor.
elements.evidence: The clause specifies “an independent Certified Public Accountant or other Audit Professional.”

elements.element: The auditor is bound by confidentiality obligations.
elements.evidence: The clause expressly requires “an auditor bound by confidentiality obligations.”

elements.element: Vendor bears the audit costs by default.
elements.evidence: The clause states that the audit cost “will be borne by Licensor” unless the stated exception applies.

elements.element: Any shift of audit costs to Customer is permitted only if an underpayment exceeds 5%.
elements.evidence: The clause shifts costs when any “discrepancy” exceeds 5%, rather than only when an underpayment exceeds 5%. This could include an overpayment or another discrepancy.

elements.element: The auditor has no direct access to Customer systems.
elements.evidence: The clause states that the audit “shall not include access to Licensee's systems.”

elements.element: Audit frequency is limited to no more than once per year.
elements.evidence: The stricter limit of no more than once in any 12-month period satisfies an annual maximum.

elements.element: Customer receives at least 15 days' notice.
elements.evidence: The clause provides the stronger protection of at least 30 days' prior written notice.

elements.element: Vendor bears the audit costs by default.
elements.evidence: The clause states that the audit cost “will be borne by Licensor” unless the stated exception applies.

elements.element: Any shift of audit costs to Customer is permitted only if an underpayment exceeds 10%.
elements.evidence: The clause shifts costs for any discrepancy exceeding 5%, so it permits cost shifting below the required 10% threshold and without requiring an underpayment.

result.reason: The audit mechanics satisfy the preferred frequency, notice, timing, auditor, confidentiality, and systems-access requirements. However, the cost-shifting trigger remains tied to any discrepancy above 5%, not an underpayment above the applicable threshold. It therefore fails both the preferred and fallback positions. The edits otherwise preserve the original audit right, but the unnecessary relocation of the cost paragraph and the unresolved trigger prevent this from being a minimal complete redline.
